title: Tenant-fenced SCIM deprovision playbook with jittered retries and RBAC v2 audit hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers report intermittent orphaned accounts after SCIM deprovision operations from SSO providers (large orgs, multi-tenant). Existing retry logic is global and causes cascading replays under tenant-wide outages; operators lack an explicit manual reconciliation flow and RBAC traces for admin actions. This ticket defines a tenant-fenced deprovisioning playbook that applies exponential backoff with bounded jitter per-tenant, integrates idempotency and audit hooks for RBAC v2, and exposes admin reconciliation controls in Console and via the internal tooling API.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Deprovision attempts are isolated per-tenant: a spike in retries from one tenant does not degrade processing for others. 2) Retry window uses exponential backoff with bounded random jitter to avoid thundering herds; parameters configurable per-tenant. 3) Each SCIM delete/update is logged with RBAC v2 metadata (actor, role, admin vs system), and stored in audit index for 90 days. 4) Console exposes a tenant-level "Reconcile SCIM" action to run a safe idempotent backfill with progress and dry-run option. 5) Manual admin reconcile operations require RBAC v2 "scim:reconcile" permission. 6) No data loss: users flagged for deprovision must either be fully removed or placed in a quarantine state with TTL, and there is a documented tombstone marker. 7) Automated tests covering success, transient network failures, and permanent 4xx errors, plus chaos-tested tenant outage scenario passed in staging.
implementation_notes:
High-level approach:
- Add tenant-scoped retry queue: when a SCIM provider request fails for user/group removal, enqueue to tenant-specific queue with metadata {tenant_id, idempotency_key, attempt, next_eta}.
- Backoff policy: base=1m, multiplier=2, cap=6h; jitter=random(0.75,1.25) applied multiplicatively. Make these parameters overridable per-tenant via config store (Console + infra flags).
- Idempotency: require idempotency_key for each SCIM operation; server persists operation state and tombstone markers to avoid double-delete races.
- Quarantine mode: for non-final failures (timeouts, 5xx), mark user as "scim_quarantine" with quarantine_ttl=7d default. Final 404/410 responses mark deletion complete.
- RBAC v2 hooks: extend SCIM service to attach actor metadata from auth token (service vs admin), include role snapshot (roles hashed) to every audit entry. Audit log format: tenant_id | resource_type | resource_id | action | outcome | actor | actor_role | attempt | idempotency_key | timestamp.
- Admin reconcile API: POST /internal/tenants/:id/scim/reconcile with options {dry_run=true,false, batch_size=500, stop_on_error=false}. Permission guarded by "scim:reconcile" scope in RBAC v2.
- Metrics: per-tenant counters for retry_count, queue_depth, last_success_ts, quarantined_users_count. Expose Prometheus metrics and per-tenant Console charts.
testing_plan: Unit tests for retry scheduler and idempotency store. Integration tests: simulate provider 502, network timeout, and 404 to validate transitions (retry vs final). Staging chaos test: rate-limit SCIM provider and assert tenant queue isolation and no cross-tenant CPU spike. E2E: run Console reconcile (dry-run) and validate audit events emitted and RBAC enforcement on sensitive routes. Load test: 10k deprovisions across 200 tenants to validate queue sharding and backoff behavior.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag the tenant-fenced retry scheduler. 2) Deploy to canary region with <5 production tenants enabled. 3) Monitor metrics (retry_count, queue_depth, error_rate) and audit logs for 48h. 4) Enable per-tenant config in Console for broader rollout in 1-week increments. 5) After full rollout, flip default quarantine_ttl and backoff settings into recommended defaults and remove feature flag after two weeks stable.
